subject: Coffee & Tea
title: Pan-Roasting: The Ancient Method
description: Learn Pan-Roasting: The Ancient Method in one minute.

hook.text: For 500 years, coffee was roasted in a simple pan over open fire—stirred by hand, judged by eye and nose.

buildup.text: Ethiopian and Yemeni coffee traditions still use this method. A flat pan over charcoal, constant hand stirring.

discovery.text: Pan roasting is inconsistent—some beans burn while others stay raw. But it's deeply personal and richly aromatic.

twist.text: In Ethiopia's coffee ceremony, guests watch the entire pan-roasting process. The smoke is fanned toward them as a welcome.

climax.text: Pan roasting connects drinkers to the transformation moment. Industrial roasting hides what pan roasting celebrates.

punchline.text: A pan, a fire, a hand. Coffee's oldest roasting method is still alive.

quiz.question: Why is pan-roasting still practiced in Ethiopian coffee ceremonies?
options: It connects drinkers to the visible transformation—the smoke is part of the welcome
